Article Title: SC asks EC to explain ‘logical discrepancy’ notices issued during Delhi SIR
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Election Commission to file its response over the basis on which persons are being issued notices under the "logical discrepancies" category during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Delhi.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya bagchi and Justice V Mohana specifically questioned the manner in which the poll panel was generating and communicating the notices.Justice Bagchi asked EC to examine whether notices were being issued mechanically and whether voters were being adequately informed about the reason for the notice. The CJI also asked the poll panel to clarify the meaning and operation of the “logical discrepancy” category.“You need to clarify logical discrepancy a little”, the CJI said.This comes after advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the petitioners, told the apex court that the problem was not merely the number of notices but the lack of clarity about what voters were being asked to establish.He said voters receiving notices were being asked to appear with documents even when the notice did not provide enough information to understand the discrepancy attributed to them.Bhushan also argued that many ordinary voters may have limited documentary records and said Aadhaar was often the principal document available to them containing their basic details. He questioned why a voter who had submitted an enumeration form and produced proof of age and residence should be required to establish additional facts.Meanwhile, advocate D S Naidu, appearing for the EC, submitted that every notice contained a reason and said the issue was not as serious as suggested by the petitioners. The poll panel also informed the top court that the 12 documents referred to in the verification process were not exhaustive.As per the petitioners, the draft electoral roll in Delhi excluded around 47 lakh names, while notices were issued to around 33 lakh other voters whose names remained in the draft roll.
Article Summary: Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya bagchi and Justice V Mohana specifically questioned the manner in which the poll panel was generating and communicating the notices. Justice Bagchi asked EC to examine whether notices were being issued mechanically and whether voters were being adequately informed about the reason.

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Tuesday attacked Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary over the harassment of a minor girl and boy in Jamui, calling for the state government’s dismissal and alleging that “maha goonda raj” was prevailing in Bihar.“The Samrat Choudhary government must be dismissed. It is a government of goons. There is ‘maha goonda raj’ in Bihar,” Raut said while reacting to the incident.The remarks came after a video purportedly showing a minor girl being groped and her male companion being assaulted by a group of youths in Jamui went viral on social media.The incident has triggered a political controversy in Bihar, with Opposition parties questioning the state government’s law-and-order record and its handling of the case.Congress leader Udit Raj also criticised the Bihar government, saying the incident reflected the deteriorating law-and-order situation in the state.Reacting to the viral video, Raj referred to previous cases involving alleged crimes against minors and questioned the government's response to such incidents.“When a murder accused is the CM of the state, it is not difficult to imagine the condition in Bihar,” Raj said, adding that law and order had deteriorated in the state.Congress MP Manoj Kumar described the Jamui incident as “one that shames humanity” and questioned the government's claims about governance and women's safety.Referring to claims that “Ram Rajya” prevailed in Bihar, Kumar asked what kind of governance was in place when an incident such as the Jamui case occurred in the state.He also referred to an earlier statement attributed to CM Samrat Choudhary that he would resign if such an incident occurred. “The current Chief Minister of Bihar used to say that if such an incident came to light, he would resign and step down from his post. I have a direct question for you: what do you have to say about this?"RJD leader and Bihar LoP Tejashwi Yadav also targeted the state government.According to ADG (Law and Order) KS Anupam, the incident took place on September 19 when the minor girl had gone to take photographs with a male friend in Jamui. A case has been registered under various sections, and three arrests have been made.

The incident has triggered a political controversy in Bihar, with Opposition parties questioning the state government’s law-and-order record.

Article Title: India sees rise in both overweight and underweight
Article Text:

Sedentary lifestyles are often blamed for rising obesity. It is perhaps the most obvious explanation, repeated ad nauseam in this digital age, where often the entire world stays within our six-inch screen. But data from the government's latest pan-India health survey (NFHS-6) suggest something quieter, and potentially more complicated for policymakers. Below-normal BMI has stopped retreating in India even as overweight and obesity rise.The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) is the government's main source of data on health and nutrition, run by the International Institute for Population Sciences for the Union health ministry. Its sixth round, NFHS-6, covered about 6.79 lakh households across 715 districts, with fieldwork running from May 2023 to December 2024. It reports 101 indicators for India and every state and union territory except Manipur.Among women aged 15-49, the share with below-normal BMI rose marginally from 18.7% in NFHS-5 to 19.7% in NFHS-6, while the share classified as overweight or obese rose steeply from 24% to 30.7%.Hence the calculated share of women in the normal-BMI range fell from 57.3% to 49.6%, a decline of 7.7 percentage points.Men aged 15-49 are moving in the same direction. Below-normal BMI rose from 16.2% to 19.7%, while overweight or obesity increased from 22.9% to 27.3%. Hence the share of men in the normal-BMI range shrank from 60.9% to 53%, a decline of 7.9 percentage points.BMI is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. For these indicators, NFHS classifies BMI below 18.5 as below normal and BMI of 25 or above as overweight or obese. It does not publish the normal range in between; TOI calculated that middle by subtracting the two published shares from 100.The NFHS-6 fact sheets are provisional, and without unit-level data it has not been tested whether the changes are statistically significant.Comparable figures for both sexes begin with NFHS-3, and below-normal BMI fell in each round until now. Among women it went from 35.6% in NFHS-3 (2005-06) to 22.9% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) and 18.7% in NFHS-5; among men, from 34.2% to 20.2% and then 16.2%.NFHS-6 is the first of these rounds in which the below-normal share rises for both sexes, and men's share, lower than women's in each earlier round, now matches it at 19.7%. Overweight has risen in every round, from 12.6% to 30.7% among women since NFHS-3 and from 9.3% to 27.3% among men.Below-normal BMI increased from NFHS-5 in 20 of the 35 state/UT comparisons among women and 27 of 35 among men. Overweight or obesity rose even more widely, in 33 of 35 among women and 28 of 35 among men. Both rose together in 19 of the comparisons for women and 20 for men.Among women, just seven of the 35 states and Union territories in the NFHS-6 release had a calculated normal-BMI share below 50% in NFHS-5; in NFHS-6, that number has risen to 16. So in 16 states, more than half of women in the 15-49 age group are either overweight or underweight. Among men, only one of the 35 — Puducherry — was below 50% in NFHS-5. In NFHS-6, 11 are below 50%.Rajasthan recorded the sharpest increase in below-normal BMI for both sexes: from 19.6% to 27.3% among women, a rise of 7.7 percentage points, and from 14% to 24.7% among men, up 10.7 points. Other large increases in low BMI among women were in Jammu & Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand; among men, the sharpest increases were in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Tripura and Delhi.At the other end, Lakshadweep saw the largest increase in overweight or obesity among women, from 33.5% to 50.1%, followed by Sikkim, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Among men, the biggest increase was in Chandigarh, from 34.4% to 48.5%, followed by Goa, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and West Bengal.The state numbers show this is not confined to a few pockets.Among urban women, 13.2% have below-normal BMI and 42.8% are overweight or obese. Among rural women, below-normal BMI is much higher at 22.5%, while overweight or obesity stands at 25.5%. Against NFHS-5, below-normal BMI among rural women has risen from 21.2%, while the urban estimate is unchanged at 13.2%. Overweight or obesity rose in both, from 33.2% to 42.8% in urban areas and from 19.7% to 25.5% in rural areas.Men show a similar urban-rural divide. Among urban men, 14.9% have below-normal BMI and 36.3% are overweight or obese. Among rural men, 21.9% have below-normal BMI and 23% are overweight or obese. Compared with NFHS-5, low BMI among urban men rose from 13% to 14.9%, while among rural men it rose more sharply, from 17.8% to 21.9%. Overweight or obesity increased from 29.8% to 36.3% in urban areas and from 19.3% to 23% in rural areas. Among men, the rise in low BMI was larger in rural India, while the increase in excess weight was sharper in urban India.Dr Sadajit Banerjee, a Kolkata-based internal medicine and geriatrics specialist, says that as an urban doctor he has been seeing mostly a shift towards overweight. Patients increasingly arrive asking about semaglutide and tirzepatide, having read about them; those whose BMI is still within acceptable limits are advised on lifestyle change instead.Most urban Indians, he says, do not seem motivated enough to exercise or change how they live, while others are frightened of the side effects of those drugs. The patients who take up either route readily are usually the ones who already have diabetes or another metabolic disorder. At population level, the coexistence of low BMI and overweight or obesity is consistent with what the World Health Organization calls the double burden of malnutrition. Low BMI is one marker of undernutrition rather than a complete measure of it.Most of the world has been moving in one direction. A 2024 Lancet analysis by the NCD Risk Factor Collaboration, covering 200 countries and territories, found obesity rising almost everywhere between 1990 and 2022 and more than a billion people living with obesity, while adult underweight fell in most countries.That is what makes the NFHS-6 reading unusual: India's overweight share is rising in line with the global pattern, but its below-normal share is not falling. A Global Burden of Disease study put India second only to China, at 180 million adults aged 25 and older with overweight or obesity in 2021. That is a modelled estimate on a different age base.The fact sheets report these BMI measures only for women, so the district picture is a picture of women. The female BMI indicators exclude women who were pregnant or had given birth in the preceding two months.Of the 713 district records in the release, 680 can be compared with NFHS-5, where both BMI figures are available for both rounds. In 372 of those 680, or 54.7%, both ends grew at once: more women with below-normal BMI, and more women overweight or obese. All districts in Punjab, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Delhi and Goa fall below 50% on the calculated female normal-BMI measure. So do the overwhelming majority in Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Haryana and Karnataka.BMI can also conceal what it is measuring. With the elderly population growing, Banerjee says he is seeing patients whose BMI is skewed by sarcopenia — too little protein and too little exercise producing muscle loss on one side and fat gain on the other. The number on the chart often stays in the normal range. Such patients may have low muscle mass and excess body fat despite an apparently normal BMI, risks that BMI alone can miss.NFHS-6 also tested blood sugar, on a different age base of 15 and above, against 15-49 for BMI. The share of women with high or very high blood sugar, above 140 mg/dl, or taking medication for diabetes rose from 13.5% to 17.8%; among men, from 15.6% to 20.9%. Urban prevalence is higher on both counts, at 21.9% among women and 23.9% among men, against 16.2% and 19.7% in rural areas.The fact sheets do not establish cause and effect.Overweight and obesity are rising fast, and low BMI has stopped retreating. Across much of the country both are now visible at the same time, which leaves public-health programmes carrying two problems rather than watching one give way to the other. For Banerjee, they are not two problems at all. "Overnourished or undernourished, both fall in the malnourished category," he says. Much of the chatter is about improving urban lifestyles. How rural India gets proper nutrition is the question policymakers will have to answer.
Article Summary: National Family Health Survey (NFHS) is the government's main source of data on health and nutrition. Its sixth round, NFHS-6, covered about 6.79 lakh households across 715 districts, with fieldwork running from May 2023 to December 2024. Below-normal BMI has stopped retreating in India even as overweight and obesity rise.

Article Title: Rajya Sabha polls: Dates announced for 12 seats in UP, Uttarakhand, Bengal
Article Text:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced the biennial elections for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, along with a by-election for one seat from West Bengal, on October 16.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Election Commission on Tuesday announced elections to 12 Rajya Sabha seats across Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal on October 16.The polls will cover 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh, one in Uttarakhand and a bypoll to one seat in West Bengal. The notification will be issued on September 29, nominations can be filed until October 6 and counting will take place on October 16, the poll panel said.In Uttar Pradesh, the members retiring include BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brijlal, BL Verma, Seema Dwivedi and Hardeep Singh Puri, Samajwadi Party leader Ram Gopal Yadav and BSP's Ramji Gautam.The seat held by former Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma has been vacant since September 11, when his resignation took effect following his appointment as lieutenant governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.In Uttarakhand, BJP member Naresh Bansal's term is also ending.Of the 10 outgoing Uttar Pradesh seats, eight are held by BJP, while the Samajwadi Party and BSP hold one each. Based on the current assembly arithmetic, BJP-led alliance is expected to win eight seats, while the Samajwadi Party could secure two.The outcome could leave BSP without representation in the Rajya Sabha as it does not have the numbers to retain Gautam's seat on its own.BSP currently has no MLA in Uttar Pradesh following the death of its lone legislator, Uma Shankar Singh, in August. The party also did not have the numbers to elect a Rajya Sabha member on its own in 2020. However, BJP had fielded only eight candidates for the 10 seats then, allowing BSP's Ramji Gautam to win.BJP is also comfortably placed to retain the Uttarakhand seat.The West Bengal bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of Rukmini Mallik, popularly known as actor Koel Mallick, on July 16. The winner will serve the remainder of the term until April 2, 2032.With a clear majority in the West Bengal Assembly, the ruling BJP is set to wrest the seat from the Trinamool Congress.
Article Summary: Election Commission announces elections to 12 Rajya Sabha seats on October 16. Polls will cover 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh, one in Uttarakhand and one in West Bengal. Members retiring include BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar and BL Verma.

NEW DELHI: High court judge RC Chavan tendered his resignation from the committee set up by the Maharashtra government to prepare a draft for the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in the state.In his resignation letter dated September 19, Chavan alleged that suggestions from members, including those on framing the questionnaire to elicit detailed public views on issues such as late marriages, infertility, unstable marriages and dispute resolution, were not considered. He also claimed that a questionnaire finalised by the chairperson had already been circulated for uploading.Chavan also flagged the involvement of an officer from outside the state in the panel."Maharashtra officers may feel they are not competent to do this duty that an officer from another state had to be called," Chavan said in his resignation letter."It may also be that he did not know as to where to fit" the officer in the committee's functioning, he added.Chavan also alleged that meetings were being concluded without substantive discussion.Agenda items such as confirmation of minutes, website modifications and finalisation of questionnaires were disposed of quickly on the directions of the chairperson, he added.Agenda items such as confirmation of minutes, website modifications and finalisation of questionnaires were disposed of quickly on the directions of the chairperson, he claimed."To solve this problem, I am vacating my seat on the committee by resigning now, so that the government can fill in the blank promptly," the former judge said.The Maharashtra government in July set up the seven-member committee, headed by retired Supreme Court Justice Ranjana Desai, to draft a framework for implementing the common civil code in the state.

NEW DELHI: IIT Bombay faculty forum president and professor Rajkumar Pant has rejected allegations against professor Suryanarayana Doolla following the death of second-year BTech student Sahil Wakode, saying the institute's SC/ST cell had no record of the student approaching it with a complaint in the months preceding his death.Pant said he spoke to IIT Bombay deputy director professor Ravindra Gudi, who confirmed that the SC/ST cell had issued a notice stating that there had been no attempt by Sahil to approach the cell in the previous three or four months.“There was absolutely no attempt by the late Sahil to approach the cell over the last three or four months. Professor Doolla did the same,” he said.Pant said Doolla had previously served as dean of student affairs before taking up his current position as dean of academic affairs and described him as someone known for being helpful to students.“To expect that a person of his nature — who is known to be very helpful to students — would do this is unreasonable,” Pant said.He said there could be situations where faculty members had to act firmly and that Doolla had acted according to the rules.“I'm personally convinced that he is not the kind of person who would indulge in these kinds of acts,” Pant said.His remarks come amid protests by IIT Bombay students following Sahil's death. Student representatives have said their protest was not intended to justify cheating or academic misconduct, but was aimed at raising concerns over institutional systems and seeking reforms.
Article Summary: IIT Bombay faculty forum president and professor Rajkumar Pant has rejected allegations against professor Suryanarayana Doolla. Article Title: ‘Global order under stress’: Jaishankar calls for stronger multilateralism at UNGA
Article Text:
EAM S Jaishankar during P4M Summit

External affairs minister S Jaishankar called for stronger multilateralism to navigate rising geopolitical tensions, conflicts and global competition, as he co-chaired the first Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace & Prosperity (P4M) Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa on Monday (local time). The summit was held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.Minister Jaishankar stressed the need for greater international cooperation and called for steps to address ongoing conflicts, create safeguards for emerging technologies and reduce risks linked to dominance and disruption. He also stressed the importance of international law, rules and norms.In a post on X, Jaishankar said the summit provided an opportunity to underline the importance of multilateralism at a time when international cooperation is facing pressure from intense competition, geopolitical tensions and conflicts.He highlighted the need to address the specific dimensions of ongoing conflicts, establish frameworks and safeguards for emerging capabilities, and reduce risks by diversifying against dominance and disruption. He also underlined the importance of international law, rules and norms.The EAM further called for “reformed multilateralism”, saying more participative discussions and transparent decision-making could help restore hope in the UN system and strengthen countries’ resolve to work together.Addressing the summit, Jaishankar thanked European Council President Antonio Costa for initiating the forum and said India was pleased to join as a co-sponsor. He said the global order was under stress, with a long-running rebalancing of the world taking a different shape amid intensifying competition, geopolitical tensions and conflicts.He said that if these pressures were left unchecked, they could undermine the spirit of international cooperation, making it crucial for multilateralism to assert itself more strongly."We meet at a time when the global order is under stress. For some decades, the world has witnessed a steady rebalancing, which was a long-expected structural evolution. However, extreme competition, geopolitical tensions, and actual conflicts have given this an entirely different character. If left unchecked, it would call into question the very spirit of international cooperation. That is why it is so essential that multilateralism asserts itself strongly at this juncture. "Jaishankar also highlighted the range of issues that he said depended on countries' willingness to cooperate, including peace and international security, climate action and climate justice, emerging technologies, development finance, countering terrorism, strengthening supply chains, disaster resilience and pandemic preparedness."At stake here are very real issues, not just words and expressions. The future of peace and international security, of climate action and climate justice, of emerging technologies and development finance, of countering terrorism and strengthening supply chains, and of ensuring disaster resilience and preparing for pandemics. All depend on a will to cooperate."The summit also saw Jaishankar make a case for Reformed Multilateralism, with participative deliberations and transparent decision-making being highlighted as ways to provide hope and optimism to the UN system and reinforce countries' resolve to work together.Meanwhile, Slovakia backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council on Monday, with foreign minister Juraj Blanár saying India, as a leading country of the Global South and an emerging power in the Indo-Pacific, should have a place at the UN's top decision-making body.Blanar's remarks came after Jaishankar participated in the first high-level Visegrád Group (V4) plus India meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York."We all agree, as V4 countries, that India, as part of the Global South, an upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as a permanent member of the UN Security Council," Blanár said.The V4 comprises Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia. The four countries held their first ministerial-level meeting with India in the new V4+India format during the UNGA high-level week.Jaishankar described the meeting as a "new historic occasion". Article Title: Who is IIT Bombay Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, removed as dean after Sahil Wakode’s death? Know his education, research and career
Article Text:
IIT Bombay suspends Professor Suryanarayana Doolla as dean after student death protests

Who is Professor Suryanarayana Doolla?

What does he research?

His teaching and academic work

His administrative roles at IIT Bombay

Why is Professor Doolla in the news now?

Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, a faculty member in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, has come into the spotlight following the death by suicide of 20-year-old BTech student Sahil Wakode and the protests that followed on the IIT Bombay campus.On September 21, IIT Bombay suspended Doolla from his administrative position as dean with immediate effect, saying further action would follow after an investigation. The institute also apologised for aspects of an earlier communication about Sahil's death, saying the circumstances surrounding the incident remained under investigation. Doolla continues to be a professor at IIT Bombay and heads the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, according to the institute's clarification.Doolla is an electrical and energy systems researcher whose work focuses on power electronics and power systems.According to his IIT Bombay profile, he completed his BTech in Electrical Engineering from Nagarjuna University in 2000, followed by an MTech in Energy Systems Engineering from IIT Bombay in 2002. He received his PhD in Power Systems from IIT Delhi in 2007.Before joining IIT Bombay, he worked with Machine 2 Machine in Hyderabad and Power Research and Development Consultants in Bengaluru.He joined IIT Bombay's Department of Energy Science and Engineering in 2009.Doolla's research is centred on the changing way electricity networks are designed and operated.His listed research interests include smart grids, microgrids, active distribution networks, power converter design and control, integration of renewable and distributed energy resources, power-system communication and energy efficiency.He has also worked on research involving microgrids and distribution systems, including projects connected with renewable energy integration. IIT Bombay's National Centre for Photovoltaic Research and Education lists him as one of its principal investigators.Doolla has taught several courses at IIT Bombay, including Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Foundation for Energy Engineering and Distributed Generation and Microgrids.His academic profile also records editorial responsibilities with journals published by organisations including IEEE and Wiley.His work has received several academic recognitions. These include the Prof. S. P. Sukhatme Excellence in Teaching Award in 2021, IIT Bombay's Excellence in Teaching Award in 2017 and the Young Faculty Award in 2009. His profile also lists a Best Paper Award at IEEE TPEC 2021 and other research and editorial recognitions.Doolla has also held several responsibilities involving students and institute administration.He served as Warden of Hostel 6 from 2012 to 2021 and later became Dean of Students Affairs in March 2023. IIT Bombay's annual report records his appointment as Dean of Students Affairs from March 3, 2023.He was also involved in the organisation of major entrance examinations. His profile lists him as Organising Chairman of JEE (Advanced) 2022, as well as Organising Chairman for CEED and UCEED that year. He had earlier served as vice chairman for JEE (Advanced), UCEED and CEED.Doolla was reportedly invigilating an examination taken by Sahil Wakode shortly before the student's death. The matter has since led to protests by IIT Bombay students.Sahil's parents have made allegations including caste-based discrimination, and a police FIR has named Doolla. These are allegations and have not been established as findings of an investigation. The institute has said further action will depend on the investigation.Students had demanded Doolla's suspension as part of an 18-point charter submitted to the institute administration. IIT Bombay subsequently removed him from his deanship, while he continues in his faculty role.The controversy has therefore brought attention to both sides of Doolla's career: his long academic and administrative association with IIT Bombay and the allegations now being examined in connection with Sahil Wakode's death.The investigation will determine the facts surrounding the case. Until then, allegations against any individual should not be treated as established findings.
Article Summary: IIT Bombay suspends Professor Suryanarayana Doolla as dean after student death protests. Doolla continues to be a professor at IIT Bombay and heads the Department of Energy Science and Engineering. His research is centred on the changing way electricity networks are designed and operated.

NEW DELHI: The large number of notices served to electors under the special intensive revision (SIR) largely stem from a key change made to SIR instructions by the Election Commission, based on its experience during SIR Phase I in Bihar. During SIR in Bihar, the rules required electors to attach documents proving their eligibility to be included in the roll, over a dozen documents were listed as acceptable proof of birth, citizenship and residence, at the enumeration stage itself.However following the uproar over the inconvenience caused to electors who may not have had these documents and thus faced exclusion, the EC revised the rules in Phase 2 covering 12 states/UTs, doing away with the requirement to submit documents with the enumeration form (EF) and instead decided to map the electors with the electoral roll from last SIR. The mapping works with inbuilt algorithms to flag logical discrepancies between the last roll and the enumeration forms, based on which notices are automatically issued.“The logical discrepancy detecting software is agnostic and does not distinguish between a VIP and a common man. The fact that election commissioner. S S Sandhu also got a notice due a discrepancy, where his name was mentioned as S S Sandhu in one place and as Sukhbir Singh Sandhu in another, proves this,” an EC functionary pointed out.“The high number of notices seems to unique to urban centres like Delhi, where the electors may have been a little casual while filling up the EF. Also, the BLOs could have been more meticulous in checking forms at the enumeration stage, as this could have cut down the discrepancies that led to the notices,” said an EC official.“If anyone does not return the EF despite three visits of the booth level officer (BLO) to his address and checking by booth level agent (BLA) of political parties, he is either absent, shifted, dead or duplicate elector and his name is not there in draft roll. ⁠If the received EF are incomplete or gives incorrect information, notices are issued.The official added that notices rarely lead to electors’ exclusion and are resolved the moment the elector presents the proof correcting the discrepancy.“No elector is excluded without a hearing, which must be followed by a speaking order, which can, after the final roll be published, be challenged first before the district election officer and then the chief electoral officer,” said an EC official.“Besides, the option of being added back to the electoral roll remains open in perpetuity. Anyone whose name is left out can always fill up Form 6, along with the declaration, on his mobile to get back into the electoral roll,” the official added.
Article Summary: The large number of notices served to electors under the special intensive revision (SIR) largely stem from a key change made to SIR instructions by the Election Commission. During SIR in Bihar, the rules required electors to attach documents proving their eligibility to be included in the roll. EC revised the rules in Phase 2 covering 12 states/UTs, doing away with the requirement to submit documents.

Article Title: Many other Shivanis: ‘Tailgated, provoked to race, shown the middle finger’ – a day in the life of women riding bikes
Article Text:
Shivani Chauhan survived a road-rage incident on Gurgaon’s Golf Course Road in which a man in a car chased her and knocked her off her moving bike.

'Danger is a tax women bikers pay on roads': Maral Yazarloo-Pattrick - Pune

‘Even in 2026, there are men who can’t seem to digest a woman on two wheels’: Neharika Yadav, Delhi

‘It feels like we are hurting the male ego just by being on the road’ — Soundari Sindy, Chennai

'While going from Gwalior to Hyderabad, a group of men followed me for 45 minutes': Atulya, Rajasthan

Patriarchal conditioning has taught men that women must be watched, judged and corrected — Devika Mehta, Noida

Just treat us like a normal rider — Riya Yadav, Gurgaon

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Her injuries will heal, but riding a bike will not be the same again for Shivani Chauhan, who survived a road rage incident in Gurgaon last week in which a man in a car chased Shivani and knocked her off her moving bike on Golf Course Road. “I don't know when I'll start riding again, but whenever I do, I'll have that fear that this can happen again – that another car can come from behind and hit me,” she says.It’s a fear women bike riders understand, and echo, because of what they describe as “unprovoked aggression” that comes their way on roads. Riders TOI spoke to described being chased, tailgated, obstructed, challenged to race and subjected to lewd gestures simply for being women on motorcycles.Delhi-based rider Neharika Yadav said men have chased her from different angles to take photographs or start conversations, while Gurgaon rider Geetika Khurana recalled an incident of men blocking her way and revving alongside her to provoke a race. Male drivers revving their engines, driving dangerously close, honking incessantly – Mumbai-based motorcycle trainer and motivational speaker Shilpa Balakrishnan (51) describes this as a “routine” experience for woman on bikes.“Many have tried to corner me when I overtake. They behave this way simply because they see a woman riding,” she says.The India Women Rider Safety and Mobility Report 2026, based on responses from 542 women riders, found that 57% had experienced harassment on the road.For Shivani (27), who started riding only two years ago, the Sept 13 incident has forever changed the “therapeutic experience” of riding her Aprilia. “The incident keeps playing on my mind on a loop every now and then. It has affected me very badly, I think it will be a long time before I’m able to pick up the bike again,” says Shivani, who had kept her biker identity a secret on social media. As ‘Sia’, she felt freedom.Neharika, a dentist based in Delhi, and Pune-based fashion designer Maral Yazarloo-Pattrick (45) can relate. “I ride a bike because it gives me joy, not because I want to prove anything to anyone. In Delhi-NCR, we get cast into a stereotype. Even in 2026, there are men who can’t seem to digest a woman coming on two wheels. Since traffic here is dense, there are men like (Kalyan) Bainsla (who attacked Shivani) who will not give space to a woman rider. They will keep instigating you. I think they get some perverse joy out of it,” she says.Yazarloo-Pattrick says danger is a tax women bikers pay on roads and freedom is the reason they keep paying it. “Such behaviour is an everyday reality. I’m shocked that anyone in India is surprised,” she says. Earlier this month, she was returning from Ladakh when she noticed a black SUV without a number plate following her. She switched on her GoPro but did not try to outrun it. Instead, she slowed down and pulled into a petrol pump. “If someone is chasing me and I cannot safely get away, I always head towards a crowded place.”Soundari Sindy, a lawyer in her mid-30s based out of Chennai, says attitude towards women riding bikes is similar across the country. “It almost feels like we are hurting the male ego just by being on the road,” she tells TOI. A professional racer, Soundari commands a 150cc bike with her 5ft 1in frame. “Snide comments are common. There are strangers who have made fun of me, saying my feet would not touch the ground,” she says.Suparna Sarkar (39), chief instructor at a motorcycle training academy in Gurgaon, tells TOI what made Shivani’s case different was that the aggression was caught on camera. “It’s just that she had a camera, so it led to widespread anger. Girls I teach biking to often share incidents where either people tried to race from behind or they were hit,” she says. Sarkar has experienced it herself. In 2023, she was riding near Mahipalpur in Delhi when a vehicle hit her. “There were no cameras in the area. I didn’t have a camera either,” she says.Sandhya Das, a 38-year-old IT professional who rides with Soundari, agrees that the sight of her on a bike is somehow “not palatable to some men”, whether she is in traditional attire or in biker gear with a jacket and gloves. “Men have tried to zip past me and tried to throw me off balance,” she says.Chetana Naik (37) from Mumbai, who twice encountered a group of make bikers intimidating and overtaking her – in Kashmir recently and in Punjab earlier – adds, “For some men, being overtaken by a woman appears to be an insult that must be avenged. They begin intimidating us till their egos are satisfied,” she says.Professional rider Anita Krishnan says even riding gear can be misread by some motorists as an invitation to race. “They start racing with you. It could be a car or even a bike. They will whizz past you at speed, trying to entice you into a race. This is very common,” she says. For long-distance riders, she points out, jackets, helmets and boots are protection from crashes, flying debris, rain, heat and cold, not racing gear.Krishnan says she sometimes tucks her hair inside her jacket so motorists cannot immediately tell that she is a woman. “The gear also camouflages whether you are a woman. If your hair is out, only then people would know you are a woman. So, I would mostly hide my hair,” she says.For 23-year-old Anainah Batiwala, camouflage goes further. The Mumbaikar does not feel comfortable riding in shorts and, after dark, goes out in baggy clothes. “I dress like a guy in baggy pants,” she says. “I wear my actual going-out clothes underneath.”Atulya (23) remembers being scared for her life a couple of years ago while travelling from Gwalior to Hyderabad. A group of men followed her bike relentlessly for about 45 minutes on the highway. “I kept riding for about 10-15km even after I lost them. I was so scared that something would happen to me if I applied the brakes,” she says.Atulya (23) remembers being scared for her life a couple of years ago while travelling from Gwalior to Hyderabad. A group of men followed her bike relentlessly for about 45 minutes on the highway. “I kept riding for about 10-15km even after I lost them. I was so scared that something would happen to me if I applied the brakes,” she says.Atulya, who is originally from Kerala but grew up in Rajasthan, has been riding her bike all over India from the age of 18. While the incident rattled her, she decided to keep going.Delhi-based biker Meenakshi says long group rides can become particularly vulnerable on the return journey because riders who set out together often disperse while heading home. “Often, we get calls from riders asking for help from passers-by, or they call us to say that two or three people are following them,” she says. Krishnan says women travelling alone or in smaller groups also become more selective about where they stop after dark and often share their live location with family members.Organised riding groups have built formal safety systems around that vulnerability. Some assign a leader at the front, a tail rider to make sure nobody is left behind, and a marshal to keep both ends connected. “Men may have the liberty to stop anywhere, but women have to take extra precaution,” says Saify Ratlamwala, who runs riding groups in Navi Mumbai.Devika Mehta, a media professional from Noida, narrates how a BMW came dangerously close to her bike on a curved road, nearly running her off.“Remarks, lewd gestures, honking, and constant stares make our freedom rides really ugly. If they don’t hit you, they will come extremely close or follow to just mess with you,” the 40-year-old says, blaming this behaviour on “generations of patriarchal conditioning that has taught men that women must be watched, judged and corrected”. “Add weak impulse control, peer bravado, lax policing and near-zero consequences and harassment starts to feel normal, even entertaining, to them,” Devika says.Geetika (25), a PR professional based in Gurgaon, said catcalling, teasing and obstructing the way are things most women riders have gone through in NCR. “The day I took my first ride, the experience was not pleasant. A group of boys obstructed my way and challenged me to race with them by coming close and revving their bikes. Since then, I’ve only taken my bike out early morning when I’m assured of encountering the least traffic. ”Sarkar says it’s “not all bad that women just can’t ride on Delhi-NCR roads”, but agreed there is a “section of people who create nuisance” and that can happen anytime. “It’s not only a women rider problem, but a women safety and road safety issue. When people are on the road, they should behave. When someone is driving a car, there is a base, there is support, it will not lose balance. But when you are on a two-wheeler, even the minutest touch will make you fall,” adds Sarkar.Though less exposed than those on two-wheelers, women who drive cars say they have also encountered a “sense of entitlement” from strangers on the road, including cab drivers.Pooja (38), who has been driving for 12 years in Delhi, says comments are common, not because she has done anything to provoke it but because it’s a woman at the wheel. “I keep getting told by strangers that the size of my car (a Scorpio) doesn’t ‘match’ mine.”Rupali, an advertising professional from Noida, says she once deliberately slowed down to let a group of men overtake her in their car, just so she wouldn’t be harassed. This did not deter them. “They stopped and waited for me to pass, rolled down the windows and showed me their middle fingers,” the 35-year-old says. After they sped off, Rupali says, she drove at 30kmph so she wouldn’t encounter them again.Yet the hostility has not stopped more women from taking up motorcycles. Meenakshi says the number of women she sees learning to ride has increased sharply. “Three years ago, if I trained 10 women in a month, the number would be 60-70 now,” she says. The profile, according to Krishnan, is changing too, with women in their 40s, 50s and even 60s increasingly taking up long-distance riding.Dnyanadaa Mhaskar is an example of that change. The Navi Mumbai schoolteacher began riding at 41, bought a motorcycle while still on a learner’s licence and, by her own account, barely knew how to work the clutch and gears. She later borrowed her grocer’s 100cc Hero for a ride to Pune and joined an all-women motorcycling group. Now 54, she says simply: “Riding is my solace and my bike is my soulmate.”Riya Yadav, a Gurgaon-based professional biker who has been riding since she was a teenager, adds, “People need to realise that we are just riding a bike. We are not doing some rocket science. Just treat us like a normal rider.”Most of these women say they have learnt to live with the unwanted attention on roads. “I think society at large has to change for us to see any meaningful change in men’s mindset towards a female driver. Till then, women need to take utmost precautions while riding. And be brave,” Shivani says.
Article Summary: India Women Rider Safety and Mobility Report 2026, based on responses from 542 women riders, found that 57% had experienced harassment on the road. Riders TOI spoke to described being chased, tailgated, obstructed, challenged to race and subjected to lewd gestures simply for being women on motorcycles.

Article Title: 4 European nations back India's bid for permanent UN seat, Jaishankar calls it 'historic'
Article Text:
Image credit: X/ Jaishankar

Jaishankar on V4's role in global affairs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India, V4 agree on closer cooperation

Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czech Republic on Monday backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, with Slovakia foreign minister Juraj Blanár saying India, as a leading country of the Global South and an emerging power in the Indo-Pacific, should have a place at the UN's top decision-making body.The remarks came after external affairs minister S Jaishankar participated in the first high-level Visegrád Group (V4) plus India meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York."We all agree, as V4 countries, that India, as part of the Global South, an upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as a permanent member of the UN Security Council," Blanár said.The V4 comprises Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia. The four countries held their first ministerial-level meeting with India in the new V4+India format during the UNGA high-level week.Jaishankar described the meeting as a "new historic occasion" and said the discussions covered political, economic, defence, technology, space, connectivity and people-to-people ties."We had our first Visegrad Four and India meeting. It was, in a sense, a new historic occasion, and I would like to thank Minister Juraj (Foreign Minister of Slovakia) for convening us today. It was a very, very productive meeting.What we agreed was that since India's relationship with the European Union itself is deepening, with the V4, we would take some special initiatives to create an annual business forum. As foreign ministers, we would meet annually. That was the consensus. We would also explore in technology and innovation whether we could be doing more. We have a very strong history with all the V4 countries in defense. We want to refresh and take forward that record and that cooperation. We discussed space issues, connectivity, and people-to-people mobility. We have students in each of the V4 countries. Overall, in terms of our cooperation, as well as a very good and useful exchange on the big global crisis, the Ukraine conflict, and what's happening in the Gulf. I think it was a very worthwhile and productive meeting. I'm very pleased about it."Asked about the political importance of the V4 for India on the global stage, Jaishankar said New Delhi viewed the four countries as partners with strong industrial, technological and innovation capabilities."We have very good relations with the V4 countries, and we know that these are countries with a very strong, very distinctive capability. They are industrial economies, economies with great innovation and technology talent. And I think how the V4 come together is for them to decide. But we certainly welcome the opportunity to work."India has been seeking reform of the UN Security Council and a permanent seat on the body. The Council currently has five permanent members, China, France, Russia, the UK and the US, alongside 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms.Jaishankar had formally launched India's campaign for a non-permanent UNSC term for 2028-29 in July, while New Delhi has continued to press for broader reform of the Council and permanent membership for India.Jaishankar said the meeting also resulted in an agreement to strengthen cooperation through annual foreign ministerial meetings and an annual business forum.In a post on X, Jaishankar said: "Our first meeting in the V4+India format agreed to: Closer political cooperation including annual meetings of Foreign Ministers. Deeper economic cooperation, including the Annual Business Forum. Reinvigorating our defence cooperation. Further development of our cultural cooperation and people-to-people relations."The meeting included Poland's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, Hungary's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Dr Anita Orbán, Slovakia's foreign minister Juraj Blanár and Czechia's foreign minister Petr Macinka.Jaishankar is leading the Indian delegation at the 81st UN General Assembly high-level week in New York and is scheduled to address the General Debate on September 26.
Article Summary: Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czech Republic back India's bid for a permanent seat on the UN Security Council. External affairs minister S Jaishankar participated in the first high-level Visegrád Group (V4) plus India meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly.

Article Title: IIT-Bombay student suicide case: Institute apologises over earlier remarks; student affairs dean suspended
Article Text:
IIT Bombay suspends Dean Suryanarayana Doolla

MUMBAI: IIT-Bombay placed Prof Suryanarayana Doolla on immediate suspension from his deanship, following continued students' protests on campus for the last three days. Prof Doolla was the dean of administrative affairs. He was accused of abetment of Sahil Wakode's death by suicide. Wakode's family also filed a case of harassment against him under the Atrocities Act. The institute issued a public apology on their social media handle, after students accused them of 'defaming' Wakode, without carrying out a detailed inquiry."We apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil," it said. "The details and circumstances leading up to the incident remain subject to investigation by the appropriate authorities. In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process," the institute added. The administration also denied the allegations of the director's resignation, after videos of him from the protest went viral.In a mail sent to the campus residents, the institute director, Prof Shireesh Kedare, mentioned, 'the deanship of Prof Suryanarayan Doolla is suspended with immediate effect. Any further action will be taken after investigation'. Doolla has not been suspended from his professorship at the energy science and engineering department.A meeting of the institute's Board of Governors is underway.The students submitted a charter of 18 demands on Sunday night in a meeting with the director and the institute functionaries, which went on for three hours. The director signed the charter. Students pressed on the suspension of Prof Doolla and an apology along with 16 other demands.In the list of demands raised by the students' groups on the campus, the students have demanded an an independent investigation committee, with student representatives and external members recommended by students, suspension of officials who are found guilty after the investigation, a fair compensation for the families.Among the many demands, the students have also sought a code of conduct and sensitisation for professors.The director signed the list of demands on the live recording, though officials refused to comment. An open house with students is expected to be scheduled today.Protests erupted on the Powai campus on Friday night after Wakode, a second-year student of energy science and engineering, ended his life hours after he was caught using a mobile phone during the institute’s mid-semester examination. He allegedly uploaded the exam paper on an AI platform for answers. This is the third case of suicide on the campus this year.While the institute, in a statement, mentioned that no action was initiated against Wakode, many claimed that he was threatened with suspension.
Article Summary: IIT Bombay suspends Dean Suryanarayana Doolla. He was accused of abetment of Sahil Wakode's death by suicide. The students submitted a charter of 18 demands on Sunday night in a meeting with the director and the institute functionaries, which went on for three hours.

NEW DELHI: Three people have been arrested on Monday by police in Bihar's Jamui district in connection with the alleged harassment of a minor boy and girl, after a video of the incident went viral on social media.While talking to media, Jamui SP Bishwajeet Dayal said the incident took place on the evening of September 19 and an SIT headed by Sub-Divisional Police Officer Deepti Monali has been formed to identify and arrest all those involved."Although the incident is two days old, no complaint was made before us by the boy or the girl till Sunday. It has triggered widespread outrage on social media and drawn reactions from political leaders.Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi called the incident "deeply disturbing".

Article Title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s big push to make state drug-free
Article Text:
Punjab Chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann

Punjab Chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann’s government has expanded its ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’ anti-drug campaign beyond a conventional police crackdown, combining action against drug networks with prevention in schools, youth engagement, community vigilance and treatment for people battling addiction.The government said the campaign seeks to make it harder to sell drugs, easier for citizens to report peddling, prevent young people from falling into addiction and ensure those affected can access timely treatment. The strategy brings police, teachers, students, community volunteers and health workers into a coordinated anti-drug effort.Between March 2025 and September 2026, Punjab’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force registered 61,824 FIRs and arrested 81,433 people. Authorities seized 3,918 kg heroin, 991 kg opium, 47 tonnes poppy husk, 1,416 kg ganja and 65 lakh tablets and capsules during the period. Punjab Police also conducted 79,293 public meetings to strengthen community participation in the campaign.The government has simultaneously taken the prevention campaign into schools. A 14-week anti-drug curriculum is being taught to 7.5 lakh students across 3,600 schools through trained teachers.In the first phase, nearly 25,000 teachers from 13 districts are being sensitised, with 7,000 already trained in Amritsar, Tarn Taran and Fazilka. The programme aims to help teachers identify early signs of mental-health distress, vulnerability to substance abuse and possible intervention.Youth programmes are also being used to address peer influence and social acceptance of drugs. Schools have been given year-long activity calendars, while colleges are promoting cultural festivals, mental-health clubs, sports and other activities to encourage healthier lifestyles and reduce the stigma around recovery.At the grassroots level, around 1.25 lakh people have joined nearly 15,000 Village and Ward Defence Committees. More than 50,000 members have been trained to use the Nasha Mukti App to report drug-related information and connect people seeking help with government services.Since its launch on March 1, 2025, the safe Punjab whatsApp helpline has received more than 51,000 citizen tip-offs, which the government said helped police make over 25,000 drug-related arrests.The government has also expanded treatment infrastructure, with Punjab currently having 547 OOAT centres, 219 de-addiction centres and 91 rehabilitation centres. Government facilities have been revamped, health workers trained and skilling and creative activities introduced at treatment centres.Admissions to government de-addiction and rehabilitation centres rose from over 12,200 in 2024 to nearly 34,000 in 2025, an increase of more than 170%, according to the government. The figures indicate a sharp rise in people seeking institutional support as Punjab seeks to combine enforcement with prevention, community action and rehabilitation in its fight against drugs.
Article Summary: Punjab’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force registered 61,824 FIRs and arrested 81,433 people. Authorities seized 3,918 kg heroin, 991 kg opium, 47 tonnes poppy husk and 1,416 kg ganja.

Article Title: Grounds in writing a must during arrests even in UAPA: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Supreme Court Friday pointed to five "evils" associated with the ban on liquor

'Court nod required for re-arrest when flouting Article 22'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner, Supreme Court on Monday held that a person's personal liberty cannot be invaded except in accordance with the procedure established by the Constitution, even if accused of a grave offence and anti-social activities, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.Elucidating Article 22 of the Constitution, which offers protection against arrest and detention in certain cases, a bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar said a person must be provided with the grounds of arrest by the probe agency at the time of arrest in writing and its language understandable to the accused. SC said this is applicable in all cases including under special laws - such as PMLA and UAPA - regardless of the nature and gravity of offence.Going a step further, the bench said that if a person's arrest is declared illegal for non-compliance with Article 22, then he or she cannot be re-arrested in the same case without approval from a senior police officer and nod from the court concerned."We need to remind ourselves that Constitution or a constitutional provision cannot be interpreted in a vacuum. Interpretation of Constitution cannot also be left to imponderables in the form of ifs and buts.Constitution is based on certain basic principles, much above the statutory threshold. Therefore, violation of Constitution or a constitutional provision cannot be countenanced. It has to be dealt with strictly. It is not dependent on the nature or gravity of the offence, encompassing within its sweep all offences. It cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner," the bench said. Referring to SC's verdict in the Prabhu Dayal Deorah case on preventive detention, the court said, "The gravity of the evil to the community resulting from anti-social activities can never furnish an adequate reason for invading the personal liberty of a citizen, except in accordance with the procedure established by Constitution and laws."The bench said that when a person is arrested, his right to liberty under Article 21 is curtailed and it is necessary that the person must understand on what grounds he has been arrested."The requirement of informing the arrested person the grounds of arrest in the light of and under Article 22(1) is not a mere formality but a mandatory binding constitutional safeguard. Thus, if a person is not informed of the grounds of his arrest as soon as may be, it would amount to violation of his fundamental rights thereby curtailing his right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 of Constitution, rendering the arrest illegal," the bench said.
Article Summary: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar said a person must be provided with the grounds of arrest by the probe agency at the time of arrest in writing and its language understandable to the accused. SC said this is applicable in all cases including under special laws - such as PMLA and UAPA.

Article Title: No median cuts, surface intersections on future high-speed NH corridors: NHAI
Article Text:
A view of the Barapullah Phase-3 elevated corridor that is scheduled to be inaugurated on September 29, 2026, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: New access-controlled high-speed national highway corridors will have no median (divider) openings and no at-grade (surface level) intersections, a move that aims at eliminating conflict points and reducing crashes.It has also been mandated under new NHAI guidelines issued on Monday that these corridors won’t have raised concrete dividers but flush medians — painted centre lanes with thick wire ropes or crash barriers. These will also have advance exit signage at 5 km, 2 km, 1 km and 500 metres to help motorists prepare for lane changes well in advance.The design provisions are aimed at improving safety on access-controlled corridors where cars are allowed to travel at speeds of up to 100 kmph. Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, Ambala-Kotputli corridor and Trans-Haryana corridor are among such highways.NHAI said the guidelines seek to bring uniformity in the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed corridors and ensure consistency in technical standards across projects.“The guidelines will apply to all upcoming four-lane and six-lane greenfield and brownfield access-controlled high-speed national highways,” an NHAI spokesperson said.Officials said eliminating median cuts and surface intersections will prevent dangerous cross movements and wrong-side driving, while standardised signage and geometric design will improve traffic flow and reduce the risk of high-speed crashes on the new generation of national highway corridors.The move is significant as govt has set a target of developing 50,000 km of access-controlled high-speed corridors over the coming years.At present, there are no separate standards governing the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed national highways, except for expressways. The new document fills that gap by laying down dedicated norms for highways that are access-controlled but not classified as expressways.The guidelines also specify lane configuration based on detailed traffic assessment and future traffic projections. Depending on the expected traffic volume and the number of structures such as bridges, flyovers and interchanges, these corridors will have a right of way of 60 metres or 70 metres.
Article Summary: Design provisions aimed at improving safety on access-controlled corridors. Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, Ambala-Kotputli corridor and Trans-Haryana corridor are among such highways. NHAI said the guidelines seek to bring uniformity in the planning and design of access- controlled high-speed corridors.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India will manufacture indigenous high-speed or bullet trains with a design speed of 350 kmph (B35) by 2030, matching Japan's next-generation E10 series trains that are scheduled for production the same year, according to the railway ministry's Cabinet proposal seeking approval for the revised cost of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project.Cabinet has approved the revised cost of the project at over Rs 2 lakh crore, nearly double the original estimate prepared in 2015, and the expenditure of nearly Rs 1 lakh crore escalated cost will come from budgetary support.TOI has learnt that the ministry informed the Cabinet it has initiated the process to develop B35 trains after the Japanese side conveyed in Dec 2024 that production of existing E5 series trains was being phased out. It mentions that Japan indicated that production of E10 trains would begin in 2030 and they would be ready for operations by 2034. Officials said deployment of E10 trains would be explored when they become available.The ministry has said that manufacturing of indigenous B28 high-speed trains has been taken up and India will also develop its own Bharat Train Control System (BTCS). The move mirrors China's indigenous CTCS signalling and train control system, which manages speed, spacing and safety across conventional and high-speed rail networks.As per the ministry, sharp increase in project cost from earlier Rs 1.1 lakh crore is largely due to a more than three-fold rise in land acquisition cost to about Rs 19,700 crore; a nearly 50% increase in infrastructure cost to over Rs 1 lakh crore, and around 100% escalation in spending on trains and signalling systems compared with the 2015 estimate.The current cost of the project, excluding future Japanese trains, works out to around Rs 399 crore per km.Initially, the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor will operate with B28 trains having a design speed of 280 kmph, while their maximum operating speed will be "249 kmph". BEML has received contracts to manufacture 32 B28 trains.Two prototype trains are expected to be ready for trial runs in the first quarter of 2027. BEML informed the BSE on Friday that it has received a separate Rs 5,400-crore contract to manufacture 15 additional B28 trains. The full 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor is targeted for completion by Dec 2030.
Article Summary: India will manufacture indigenous high-speed or bullet trains with a design speed of 350 kmph (B35) The railway ministry's Cabinet proposal seeking approval for the revised cost of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project. Cabinet has approved revised cost at over Rs 2 lakh crore, nearly double original estimate.

Article Title: Govt staff outside CGHS areas can now opt for scheme
Article Text:
Central government employees living or posted outside the CGHS-covered area can now make a one-time choice to join the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), even if there is no CGHS Wellness Centre in their city.

NEW DELHI: Central government employees living or posted outside the CGHS-covered area can now make a one-time choice to join the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), even if there is no CGHS Wellness Centre in their city.The Union health ministry has removed the geographical restriction that earlier prevented eligible employees outside the prescribed CGHS area from opting for the scheme. The move will benefit employees residing or posted outside the prescribed coverage area.Earlier, an employee’s eligibility for CGHS depended on where they lived or were posted. Where a 5-km limit was prescribed, coverage was linked to the area around a CGHS Wellness Centre. Employees outside the prescribed area could not opt for CGHS.Under the new rule, an eligible employee residing or posted outside the CGHS-covered area can opt for the scheme by paying the prescribed CGHS contribution and meeting the other eligibility conditions.However, the choice is a one-time decision and will be final and binding. It will also apply to all eligible dependents of the employee.Employees opting for CGHS cannot simultaneously claim medical benefits under the Central Services (Medical Attendance) Rules, 1944.Their eligible family members will also have to be covered under the same system.The employee will have to continue paying the prescribed CGHS subscription irrespective of where they subsequently reside or are posted. No travelling or daily allowance will be admissible for treatment or procurement of medicines under CGHS.The new provision does not give employees already residing or posted within a CGHS-covered area the option to shift from CGHS to medical facilities under the CS(MA) Rules.Employees who do not exercise the new option will continue to be governed by the CS(MA) Rules, wherever applicable.The new provisions have come into force with immediate effect. The ministry has issued an option and undertaking form for employees who wish to opt for CGHS.
Article Summary: Central government employees living or posted outside the CGHS-covered area can now make a one-time choice to join the Central Government Health Scheme. The Union health ministry has removed the geographical restriction that earlier prevented eligible employees outside the prescribed CGHS area from opting for the scheme.

Article Title: Hospitals told to report serious medical device events within 15 days
Article Text:
​IPC has issued a new guidance document asking hospitals to strengthen monitoring and reporting of adverse events linked to medical devices. (AI-generated image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A faulty insulin pump that delivers too much insulin, an infusion pump that gives medicines too quickly, a pulse oximeter showing incorrect oxygen levels or a defibrillator failing during a cardiac emergency will now come under a more systematic hospital safety-monitoring system.The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC) has issued a new guidance document asking hospitals to strengthen monitoring and reporting of adverse events linked to medical devices. Serious adverse events have to be reported to the Materiovigilance Programme of India (MvPI) within 15 days, while non-serious adverse events and certain potentially harmful near-miss incidents have to be reported within 30 days.Patients too have a direct role. Those who notice that a medical device is not functioning properly or experience an adverse event can inform the treating hospital or healthcare professional and directly report suspected device-related events to IPC.IPC has provided a toll-free helpline, 1800-180-3024, for consumers and other stakeholders. It supports reporting in 10 languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam.Importantly, the system is not limited to cases in which a patient is actually injured. A device malfunction or quality problem detected before use can be treated as a near miss. If it could potentially cause harm during future use, it is reportable within 30 days even when no patient has been harmed.The guidance also says suspected device-related events should be reported even when it has not yet been established that the device caused the problem, allowing the event to be assessed and investigated further.The guidance, prepared by IPC in collaboration with the World Health Organization India and other stakeholders, covers medical devices including in-vitro diagnostic devices, implants, life-support equipment and newer artificial intelligence-enabled and software-based devices.Hospitals have been asked to actively monitor critical devices, including invasive, implantable and life-supporting equipment. Their performance, malfunctions, complaints and near misses should be reviewed weekly or monthly based on usage and risk, with heightened monitoring of devices under IPC safety alerts or advisories.Each department should have a designated nodal person for monitoring, staff sensitisation and timely reporting. Lists of monitored devices should be displayed in intensive care units, operation theatres, catheterisation laboratories and specialty wards.The guidance was unveiled on Monday by Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel during National Pharmacovigilance Week. The government also announced approval of the Biovigilance Programme of India, under which IPC will lead monitoring of adverse events associated with medicines and biological products used in organ and tissue transplantation.
Article Summary: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC) has issued a new guidance document asking hospitals to strengthen monitoring and reporting of adverse events linked to medical devices. Serious adverse events have to be reported to the Materiovigilance Programme of India within 15 days. Non-serious adverse events and certain potentially harmful near-miss incidents must be reported within 30 days.

Article Title: WHO puts stroke, cancer, mental health on 10-year traditional medicine research agenda
Article Text:
The World Health Organization has identified major health conditions for research into traditional, complementary and integrative medicine over the next decade. (Photo: @WHO)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From stroke and cancer to mental health and pain management, the World Health Organization has identified major health conditions for research into traditional, complementary and integrative medicine over the next decade.Its 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders, and reproductive health and childbirth as priority areas. Prevention and health promotion, healthy ageing and healthy childhood are also included.The report highlights a striking mismatch between disease burden and research. Stroke ranks third globally in causes of mortality and disability, yet less than 1% of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine-funded grants address the condition. Mental health ranks eighth among contributors to disability-adjusted life years, but the review found very few or no grants specifically focused on mental health conditions. Musculoskeletal conditions are also a prominent cause of disability globally but remain under-researched relative to their burden.Cancer, too, features among the priority areas, with the report noting rising global incidence and calling for research into integrative oncology and palliative care.For metabolic health and endocrine disorders, WHO identifies the need for stronger evidence, including longer-term studies on conditions such as type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome.WHO says the aim is to generate stronger evidence on effectiveness, safety, regulation and health-system integration so countries can make informed decisions about the role of these approaches in healthcareThe research agenda also puts patient safety under the spotlight. It calls for studies on herb-drug interactions, monitoring and reporting of adverse events, regulatory and quality-assurance systems, and the safe integration of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine into primary healthcare.The push comes against a broader funding gap. WHO says traditional, complementary and integrative medicine is widely used globally, with use reaching up to 80% of populations in some settings, while less than 1% of global health research funding is directed towards research in the field.India has a direct connection to the agenda. The WHO report acknowledges financial support from the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, for its development and publication. India was also among the health ministries that participated in the Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine, held in New Delhi in December 2025.The report, however, is a research-prioritisation framework rather than a clinical guideline or recommendation to use any particular traditional medicine.
Article Summary: The 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders, and reproductive health and childbirth as priority areas. Prevention and health promotion, healthy ageing and healthy childhood are also included. Stroke ranks third globally in causes of mortality and disability.

Article Title: Animal shelters to cost 7,000 crore, can't build them, NHAI tells SC
Article Text:
An additional financial burden of Rs 7,000 crore wo- uld be imposed on NHAI in creating and managing the shelters

New Delhi: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) Monday moved SC seeking to absolve it from the court-assigned responsibility of creating infrastructure along 72,000-km network of national highways (NHs) to shelter stray cattle and animals, which are increasingly causing accidents.Seeking an urgent hearing on NHAI's application, solicitor general Tushar Mehta asked a bench led by CJI Surya Kant to list it before a special bench headed by Justice Vikram Nath, which had directed NHAI to coordinate with states on removal of stray cattle and animals and keeping them in shelters across India alongside NHs. "Neither does the statute cast such a responsibility on NHAI nor does it have the expertise to create shelters across the 72,000-km stretch of NHs and an additional financial burden of Rs 7,000 crore would be imposed on it in creating and managing these shelters," SG Tushar Mehta said.
Article Summary: NHAI seeks to absolve it from court-assigned responsibility of creating infrastructure along 72,000-km network of national highways. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta asked a bench led by CJI Surya Kant to list it before a special bench headed by Justice Vikram Nath.

Article Title: Courts must not interfere in cop probe: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday said investigation of a crime was the police's exclusive domain and should be left to the investigating agency's discretion, and courts should not interfere to decide when a probe should stop.Quashing a Bombay High Court order which had refused to grant an extension of time to file a chargesheet against a Popular Front of India (PFI) member, after which the accused were granted default bail, a bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar said the HC committed an error in not granting more time to the anti-terrorism squad of Mumbai police to complete the probe."Investigation of a crime is the exclusive domain of the police. It is not the jurisdiction of the court to decide when the investigation in a case should stop. It must be left to the discretion of the investigating agency to decide the course of investigation and to proceed in its own manner. The court cannot curtail the statutory powers vested in the police except in an exceptional case on facts or where there is a statutory bar to carry out investigation by the police," the bench said.It added that courts cannot interfere with the statutory right of the police to investigate the circumstances of a cognisable crime and it was the bounden duty of the executive, through the police department, to investigate the offence and bring the offender to book."The probe agency sought time to analyse how data retrieved from mobiles, computers and other gadgets seized from the accused connect them with the terrorist activities intended to undermine the sovereignty of India. The agency is also required to indicate how the flow of money in the bank accounts of the accused connects them with the terrorist activities." SC quashed the default bail granted to the accused and asked them to surrender within 30 days.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes Bombay High Court order which refused to grant an extension of time to file a chargesheet against a Popular Front of India member. Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar said the HC committed an error in not granting more time to the anti-terrorism squad of Mumbai police to complete the probe.

Article Title: Court junks rejection of petition to probe Sonia voter roll entry
Article Text:
