NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has set aside a 2025 magisterial order rejecting a plea to probe alleged irregularities in the inclusion of Sonia Gandhi's name in the electoral rolls. It observed that the "impugned order suffers from manifest errors in law".Special judge Vishal Gogne of Dwarka courts remanded the matter to the ACJM for a fresh, reasoned order after an inquiry and after hearing the concerned police officer. It will be listed on Sept 29. He said the order was "non-speaking" and lacked reasons. There was no discussion on the sequence of Sonia's inclusion, deletion and re-inclusion in the electoral rolls of 1980, 1982 and 1983, he said. Advocate Vikas Tripathi's complaint alleged that Sonia's name was unlawfully entered in the electoral roll for New Delhi parliamentary constituency in 1980, before she acquired Indian citizenship.Her name was allegedly deleted in 1982 and re-entered in 1983, with the complaint claiming the re-entry, too, preceded her acquisition of citizenship on April 30, 1983.In 2025, ACJM dismissed the complaint as "based on bald assertions unaccompanied by essential particulars of cheating and forgery" and described the material as the "photocopy of the photocopy of the uncertified electoral roll of 1980". Tripathi challenged the order before sessions court in Dec 2025. On Monday, Gogne said such an allegation of "tampering with the electoral rules, fraudulent inclusion of the name of a voter, inclusion of the name of a non-citizen and possible use of false declaration" merits a "reasoned order" on whether cheating and forgery were disclosed.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has set aside a 2025 magisterial order rejecting a plea to probe alleged irregularities in the inclusion of Sonia Gandhi's name in the electoral rolls. It observed that the "impugned order suffers from manifest errors in law" Special judge Vishal Gogne of Dwarka courts remanded the matter to the ACJM for a fresh, reasoned order.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami says strong cooperatives, M-PACS can strengthen rural economy
Article Text:

DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday said strengthening cooperatives and M-PACS can play a key role in boosting the rural economy, supporting mountain agriculture and creating opportunities for youth in the state.Virtually addressing the inaugural session of the Shri Laxmanrao Inamdar Second Cooperative Leadership Training Programme at Pantnagar, Dhami stressed the need for skilled leadership to make cooperatives an effective instrument of economic empowerment.The programme was organised by Sahakar Bharati Uttarakhand at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar.Paying tribute to Sahakar Bharati founder Shri Laxmanrao Inamdar on his birth anniversary, CM Dhami said such training programmes would play an important role in strengthening the rural economy by empowering the cooperative sector.He said, "Strong leadership will strengthen M-PACS, strong M-PACS will strengthen villages, and strong villages will make Uttarakhand prosperous."The chief minister said several important initiatives aimed at giving a new direction to the cooperative movement had been launched from Pantnagar, the land of knowledge. The launch of the Sahakar Granth, the Devbhoomi Sarathi initiative of the State Cooperative Federation, new courses in the cooperative sector, a social media reels campaign to connect youth with cooperatives, and the M-PACS leadership training programme would give fresh momentum to the cooperative sector, he said.CM Dhami said the state government is committed to taking Uttarakhand rapidly forward towards the vision of "Samriddhi through Cooperatives".He said cooperatives can serve as an effective means of addressing several challenges faced by the hill state, including migration, strengthening mountain agriculture, providing markets for local products and boosting the rural economy.He said primary agricultural cooperative societies (PACS) are an important pillar of the state's cooperative system and are being strengthened as M-PACS to make them more capable and effective in line with changing requirements.The state government is working to provide better facilities to farmers through M-PACS, create new opportunities for youth and strengthen rural areas economically, he added.The chief minister said skilled and visionary leadership is essential to make M-PACS more effective, and the leadership training programme has been launched with this objective. Training, he said, is not merely a means of enhancing knowledge but also a powerful tool for developing new perspectives, approaches and direction among leaders.CM Dhami said connecting farmers, youth and women with the cooperative movement is a priority of the state government. The government is working to make cooperatives not merely limited to societies, but an effective instrument of public participation and economic empowerment, he said.He called upon the representatives participating in the training programme to further strengthen the spirit of cooperation in their respective areas and encourage more people to join the movement.He said all stakeholders must work together to make cooperatives a people's movement, strengthen villages, create opportunities for youth and enhance the economic strength of farmers.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami says strong cooperatives, M-PACS can strengthen rural economy. He was addressing the inaugural session of the Shri Laxmanrao Inamdar Second Cooperative Leadership Training Programme at Pantnagar.

Article Title: The 'chosen one' for a role in BSP is Ishan: Mayawati's latest U-turn in ongoing family drama
Article Text:
Mayawati’s chosen one is Ishan Anand.

A warning for Ishan

Niece loses the race

Doors forever closed for Akash Anand?

Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.

The Kanshi Ram reference

The Ambedkar example

Road ahead for Ishan

NEW DELHI: Mayawati’s chosen one is Ishan Anand. Or is he? Well, at least for now. There’s another twist in the ongoing succession drama in the BSP chief’s family. Younger nephew Ishan, who was ruled out from getting any position in the BSP only ten days back, has ended up winning Mayawati’s “trust test” for a role in the party.“Only Shri Ishan Anand from Shri Anand Kumar’s family will now be promoted by giving him a respectable responsibility in the party,” Mayawati announced on X on Sunday.So, when the BSP holds its national-level meeting in Lucknow on September 23, Ishan is likely to get a “respectable responsibility” in the party. This will be 20 days after his elder brother Akash Anand was shown the door at a similar meeting held on September 3. Ishan, Akash and their sister Deepika are children of Mayawati’s younger brother Anand Kumar, who has been “working in Mayawati’s service for many years.”But Ishan’s promotion comes with a strict rider. He has to “rise above attachment to his brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication.”There was a clear and strong warning for Ishan. “If he commits any serious act against the party, he too will be shown the door from the party.But in such a situation, no other member of Shri Anand Kumar’s family will be given any responsibility, big or small, in the party,” Mayawati announced.In a long post on X on September 12, the BSP chief had ruled out any political role for her nephews Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, but left room for Deepika to take on responsibilities in the party if the need arises.The BSP chief had said, "Today it is my final decision and pledge that in return, none of his sons, in particular, will be allowed to engage in politics by holding any position, big or small, within the BSP. If Anand Kumar, while remaining with me, needs another member to assist him, then in the current political situation, he can seek the help of his only daughter, Kumari Deepika Anand, who is currently studying law. He can then, based on her honesty, loyalty, and efficiency, assign her his own responsibilities within the party as needed. "But that did not happen.In her post, Mayawati dwelled on the “dilemma” she faced in making the decision and also shared the yardstick she used to decide the “chosen one.”“The question of who from Shri Anand Kumar’s family I should or should not promote in the party has been a matter of considerable dilemma for me for some time. Bringing this dilemma to an end, and after giving serious thought to every aspect, I have now decided that if any member of his family is to be promoted in the party, it should be someone who does not follow Akash’s footsteps in any way.”“As for seeking help from his daughter in the future, after she gets married, if her case also turns out to be like Shri Akash Anand’s, that too would not be in the interest of the party. Keeping such a possibility in mind, it would now be appropriate in the interest of the party to completely keep Shri Akash Anand and his sister away from being given any responsibility in the party. In other words, there will be no change whatsoever in this decision,” Mayawati wrote in her post.Akash Anand, who was groomed for years and, at least on two occasions in the past, announced as Mayawati’s “political successor,” now seems completely out of the picture. At least for now.“On special request of Shri Anand Kumar, I had to promote his elder son, Shri Akash Anand, in politics. Since his marriage, however, Shri Akash Anand’s conduct and activities at every step have been such that, a few days ago, I once again had to separate him from the party,” Mayawati said in her latest post.“In other words, he is now completely caught up in the web of his father-in-law, Shri Ashok Siddharth. Bringing him back into the party now would amount to a major betrayal of the party, and I can never commit such an act against the party,” she wrote.Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra. The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.Mayawati appointed him BSP’s national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him. Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.However, now with his younger brother taking the centre stage, it may not be easy for Akash to claw back into the power structure.The BSP chief shared her mantra for success in politics. “I want to tell the people of the party that, keeping my own experience in mind, if they want to succeed in politics and do something for society, they must, like me, rise above their attachment to their brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication,” Mayawati wrote in the post.She then referred to the role of BSP founder Kanshi Ram in showing her the path“The founder and architect of the BSP, respected Shri Kanshi Ram ji, after entering politics, always kept himself away from giving political benefits to his close relatives and family members. He allowed them to work in the party organisation only with a selfless spirit. Not only this, he devoted his entire life to the interests and welfare of the ‘Bahujan Samaj’, without creating a family of his own,” Maywati wrote.“Inspired by him, I too decided to follow in his footsteps and devoted my entire life to the ‘Bahujan Samaj’. However, because I am a woman, I was compelled to always keep one of my brothers or sisters with me. Under this arrangement, my younger brother, Shri Anand Kumar, has been working in my service for many years,” the BSP chief said.Justifying her move, Mayawati wrote, “I have taken this decision in the interest of the party and the movement, inspired by respected Shri Kanshi Ram ji and influenced by a letter written by the revered Baba Saheb Dr BR Ambedkar.”The BSP chief stated that Baba Saheb Dr BR Ambedkar had written a letter on February 23, 1956, warning his son Yashwant B Ambedkar over his alleged attempts to try and take control of the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press.To convey her message to Ishan and others, Mayawati cited the strong stand taken by Ambedkar against his son, “I have to inform you that I have received several communications from Shri Upsham saying that you are not allowing him to perform his duties as the accountant and cashier of the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press. You seem to think that by doing this you will take control of the press. I am warning you that the press is public property; it belongs neither to you nor to me, and it is not possible to permit any kind of irregularity in a public account.Your conduct has not been proper... If you do not heed my final and last instructions, I will remove you from the press and, if you do not heed this warning, I will also prosecute you.”‘Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown’: Well, that’s perhaps how one can describe Ishan’s future in BSP. We will have to wait and see what respectable role he gets from Mayawati on September 23 when the party meets. However, irrespective of the role, the road ahead for Ishan would be challenging.
Article Summary: BSP chief Mayawati's chosen one is Ishan Anand, at least for now. Ishan's promotion comes with a strict rider. He has to “rise above attachment to his brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication”

Article Title: 'BJP's Punjab conspiracy exposed': Sanjay Singh alleges drug trafficker Jagga was called 'Bhai' by BJP, being portrayed as revolutionary
Article Text:
"BJP’s Punjab conspiracy exposed": Sanjay Singh alleges drug trafficker Jagga was called ‘Bhai’ by BJP, being portrayed as revolutionary

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Aam Aadmi Party on Monday alleged a conspiracy by the BJP, ShiromAkali Dal and Congress to defame Punjab and undermine the Bhagwant Mann government's campaign against drugs.Senior party leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh said Jagga Singh, whom the BJP has referred to as its "bhai", has nine cases registered against him, including under the NDPS (Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances) Act, while eight cases are registered against Mohan Jeet Singh.Addressing a press conference at the AAP headquarters on Monday, Singh said that the BJP, Congress and Akali Dal are jointly hatching a deep conspiracy in Punjab."A complete conspiracy is being planned to defame the campaign being run by CM Bhagwant Mann and the AAP government against drugs in Punjab, weaken it, stop it, and ensure that Punjab is defamed across the world for drugs," he added.The AAP MP added, "There are three characters in this conspiracy, Jagga Singh, Mohanjeet Singh and Gulzar Singh. The Congress, BJP and Akali Dal, without knowing the truth or conducting any investigation, are using these people and standing behind them to make bizarre statements and run campaigns against the AAP government."Sanjay Singh said that Jagga Singh, whom the BJP and Congress are presenting as a revolutionary and claiming was running a campaign against drugs and was forced to consume poison as a result, has nine cases registered against him."Jagga Singh has already been convicted in four of these nine cases, and cases of rape, kidnapping and drug trafficking are also registered against him," he added.He continued, "Two gram panchayats had formally passed resolutions against drugs, because his business was unable to operate, as he himself had been involved in the drug trade. The Congress, BJP and Akali Dal are portraying him as a revolutionary and claiming that the government is harassing him."The AAP MP highlighted that the second person is Mohanjeet Singh, who had shown a black flag to Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann. He said the Congress, BJP and Akali Dal are running a campaign claiming that this warrior fighting against drugs was brutally beaten merely for showing a black flag. The reality, he said, is that eight FIRs are registered against Mohanjeet Singh."The third name is Gulzar, about whom it was claimed that he took his own life because of Minister Harpal Singh Cheema. The reality is that opposition parties in Punjab kept making Gulzar record videos and drove him around in a car until he made a statement against the AAP. In the first video Gulzar recorded, he did not mention Harpal Singh Cheema or the AAP. However, in a subsequent video, he named Harpal Singh Cheema. This shows that opposition parties pressured and used him, which led to his present condition," Singh said.He said, "I want to tell the Congress, BJP and Akali Dal not to indulge in such filthy politics and not to try to defame Punjab by making baseless and false allegations. The AAP government is running its campaign against drugs with complete commitment and is eliminating drugs."Sanjay Singh said that he was also aware of the period when drug mafias had links with leaders of the Akali Dal and BJP. He said the Akali Dal, BJP and Congress had together conducted the drug trade in Punjab and committed the sin of delivering drugs to every village."Sanjay Singh claimed that under the rule of these parties, the drug trade continued to flourish and governments provided protection to drug dealers."Punjab has also witnessed a period when, under the Akali Dal-BJP government, young children studying in high school and intermediate classes died because of drugs," he added."Drugs worth Rs 20,000 crore were seized at Adani's Mundra Port in BJP-ruled Gujarat. This was stated by the central government agency NIA. The NIA had approached the Supreme Court to oppose the bail of those arrested in connection with the drug trade. While opposing their bail, the NIA stated in an affidavit that the money from the drugs worth Rs 20,000 crore seized at Adani's port in Gujarat was spent on training terrorists in Pakistan," Singh said."The NIA has submitted a written affidavit before the Supreme Court opposing bail for the accused, stating that they should not be granted bail because they were very serious criminals and the money from the drugs was being used to train terrorists in Pakistan," the MP added.He noted, "Gujarat has a liquor ban and alcohol is completely prohibited there, yet 100 people died after consuming poisonous liquor, while PM Narendra Modi and Nitin Nabin did not utter a single word. In neighbouring Uttar Pradesh, 105 people died after consuming poisonous liquor in Aligarh, but not a single BJP leader said a word."Therefore, he said, BJP leaders should not try to defame Punjab, because the entire country knows them and they will be exposed across the country.Singh concluded by highlighting that the Akali Dal, BJP and Congress have themselves run the largest drug trade in Punjab. If any party has genuinely taken action against it, he said, it is the AAP and the Bhagwant Mann government."If these parties want to speak openly about this issue, we will do so, but we will not allow them to defame Punjab. Those who themselves are disgraced and against whom cases of rape, kidnapping and drug trafficking are registered are being used by these parties for politics, with the parties standing behind them," he said.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party alleges a conspiracy by the BJP, ShiromAkali Dal and Congress to defame Punjab and undermine the Bhagwant Mann government's campaign against drugs. Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh said Jagga Singh, whom the BJP has referred to as its "bhai", has nine cases registered against him.

Article Title: 'Politics was plagued by dynasties, casteism': CM Yogi takes swipe at opposition parties
Article Text:
File photo: Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MEERUT: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday launched an attack against the opposition parties, accusing them of dynastic politics and casteism.Addressing the Shakti Kendra Sanyojak Sammelan in Meerut, the CM said, "For a long time, politics was plagued by the maladies of dynastic politics and casteism. The Congress party and its political allies long treated politics merely as a vehicle for dynastic interests and personal gain. Instead of serving as a means for public service, power became a tool for them to perpetuate dynastic rule and advance their own vested interests."CM Yogi said the very name 'Shakti Kendra' defines its work. "In BJP's organisational structure, the Shakti Kendra Sanyojak embodies the entire strength of the organisation and elections," he said."Politics came to be seen as a means to serve one's own interests. BJP has presented a different ideal before this political thinking - Rashtra Pratham. For us, politics is not just a means to attain power but a medium of national service. Our workers' goal is to keep organisation above self, society above organisation and nation above society," he said.Taking a swipe at the "mujhe kya" (what's in it for me) mindset, he termed it "Manthara-buddhi"."Those who say 'mujhe kya' have Manthara-buddhi - meaning 'what will I get, no matter who does what, what is it to me?' This thinking not only harms the individual but the entire society. It creates an identity crisis, makes society flee from its responsibilities, and hampers development," he said.CM Yogi said this mindset had weakened the country and created an identity crisis, but the transformation was visible after 2014 when Prime Minister Narendra Modi assumed office."We saw a new India - an India which is proud of its heritage and sets its own speed for development. An India which no longer has an identity crisis, which walks with its chest high and looks the world in the eye. And when someone dares to challenge India, it also knows how to protect its security and sovereignty," he said.He said 'New India' under PM Modi was shedding the slave mentality and restoring pride in its heritage, citing the construction of Kashi Vishwanath Dham in Varanasi and the grand Ram Mandir in Ayodhya as examples of works once considered impossible."In Mathura-Vrindavan, development works are underway. We have taken up rejuvenation of Shuktirth, the Bhagwat land, and have also allocated funds for Vidur Koti," he added.He said the convention was aimed at awakening the strength of workers and channelising it for the party with the spirit of 'Nation First' to realise PM Narendra Modi's resolve to build an Atmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat.He welcomed BJP National President Nitin Nabin, who was present for the two-day tour of the western region, along with the state president, Union Minister Pankaj Chaudhary, national office bearers and regional leaders.The chief minister also said Uttar Pradesh's identity had changed since 2017. "There was a time when UP was counted among BIMARU states, youth did not get jobs, and people hesitated to reveal their identity. Today no one can call UP a BIMARU state. When big economies are discussed, UP's name is taken prominently," he said.Highlighting his government's achievements, he said nine and a half lakh government jobs were given, traditional enterprises were revived under 'One District One Product' (ODOP), providing employment to 3.25 crore youth, and Meerut's products, Agra's papad and Muzaffarnagar's jaggery were given national branding."Before 2017, UP was identified with 'katta and tamancha'. Now the 12-lane expressway, Namo Bharat rapid rail between Delhi and Meerut, India's largest airport - Noida International Airport - an hour away, UP's first sports university named after Major Dhyan Chand in Meerut, a film city, medical device park, semiconductor units are coming up. Sixty percent of electronic components and 55 percent of mobile phones made in India are now made in UP," he said.He said the state had become riot-free and curfew-free, ensuring the safety of daughters and traders.Alleging that those who indulged in appeasement and patronised mafias did not like this transformation, he cautioned workers against attempts to divide society on caste lines."Mahapurush do not belong to one caste; they belong to the entire society and nation. Maharana Pratap, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Guru Gobind Singh ji Maharaj are our national heroes. They cannot be tied in caste brackets," he said, adding that his government had honoured heroes of the 1857 First War of Independence.Asking workers to become 'sarathi' like Lord Krishna in the Mahabharata, he said, "History never honoured Shakuni and Manthara, but it has honoured a sarathi like Krishna for ages. Every worker should work with the feeling - my work is for Nation First."CM Yogi's attack against Congress and the opposition comes ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly election, where the BJP-led NDA eyes a third consecutive win.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath accuses opposition parties of dynastic politics and casteism. He was addressing the Shakti Kendra Sanyojak Sammelan in Meerut. The chief minister also said Uttar Pradesh's identity had changed since 2017.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi on Monday alleged that a convoy of party leaders, including himself, was pelted with stones in Assam by people he described as “BJP workers."Gogoi, who is from Assam, said former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel and Sivamoni Bora, the party’s candidate for the upcoming Nagaon Lok Sabha seat bypoll, were also among those targeted."This is the state of the car belonging to the Congress candidate Smt. Election Commission of India will not order any transfers or suspensions,” the Assam Congress president added.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal also hit out at the BJP, accusing Sarma, a former Congress leader, of sending “goons” to target political rivals.“Launching a brutal stone pelting attack on our Assam In-Charge, Ex. Article Title: ‘PM Modi assured me’: OP Rajbhar’s claim on UP division revives decades-old debate
Article Text:
UP minister OP Rajbhar (File photo)

When Mayawati proposed carving out four states from UP

Why Uttar Pradesh matters

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured him that the state would be divided into four parts, reviving a nearly two-decade-old debate over dividing the country's most populous state.Rajbhar, who heads BJP ally Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), claimed that PM Modi told him Uttar Pradesh could be divided after the caste census.“We want to assure you regarding the 27% reservation. I spoke with the prime minister about this,” he told the audience at an SBSP programme in Deoria on Sunday.“He (PM Modi) said, ‘Om Prakash ji, your point is justified, but some people are opposing it.’ I asked him how we could move forward, and he replied, ‘I will conduct a caste census, and once we have counted the castes, there will be no difficulty.’ The state will be divided into four parts. And on the day the Purvanchal is formed, if the chief minister is to be from any caste, then a Rajbhar’s son will become the chief minister,” he added.However, another UP minister and BJP ally, Sanjay Nishad, dismissed Rajbhar’s remarks as “misleading”, saying the Nishad Party was not in favour of a reorganisation.“There had been a demand to divide UP earlier, but now the state is progressing rapidly in all spheres.Further, special development funds have been allocated for regions like Bundelkhand and Purvanchal that needed handholding,” Nishad told PTI.Rajbhar has advocated the division of Uttar Pradesh in the past as well, saying in October 2018 that the “state can be developed only after it is divided into four parts.”With the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due in early 2027, Rajbhar’s remarks have revived the long-running political debate over dividing the state.Ahead of the 2012 UP assembly elections, then chief minister Mayawati revived the demand, with the state assembly passing a resolution to split Uttar Pradesh into Avadh Pradesh, Purvanchal, Bundelkhand and Paschim Pradesh.In 2011, her government had sent a proposal to the Congress-led Centre seeking the creation of the four states.Before that, in 2008, Mayawati had proposed dividing Uttar Pradesh into three parts.Several parties, including the Rashtriya Lok Dal and Congress, have also backed demands for dividing the state at various points. There have additionally been calls for a separate Bundelkhand comprising parts of Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring Madhya Pradesh.Uttar Pradesh was last divided in 2000, when the BJP-led central government carved out Uttarakhand, then known as Uttaranchal.With a population of around 25 crore, Uttar Pradesh is India’s most populous state. If it were an independent country, its population would make it the fifth- or sixth-most populous country in the world.Geographically, Uttar Pradesh is the fourth-largest state in India.It sends 80 members to the 543-seat Lok Sabha, the highest representation of any state or Union territory. Its legislative assembly has 403 members.Six prime ministers were born in Uttar Pradesh, while several others, including Narendra Modi, have represented the state in Parliament.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh was last divided in 2000, when the BJP-led central government carved out Uttarakhand, then known as Uttaranchal. With a population of around 25 crore, Uttar Pradesh is India’s most populous state. If it were an independent country, its population would make it the fifth or sixth-most populous country in the world.

Article Title: Nandigram bypoll: Congress candidate Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 5 in 2007 agitation case
Article Text:
Congress nominee Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 5

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Congress' Nandigram bypoll nominee Milan Pradhan was on Monday remanded to judicial custody till October 5 in connection with a case registered at Khejuri Police Station 19 years ago, dealing a setback to his campaign for the October 6 assembly bypoll.Pradhan was sent to judicial custody by a Contai court in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district, his counsel Ayan Bhattacharjee said. He added that the order would be challenged before the Calcutta high court.The development came two days after a Haldia court had remanded Pradhan to judicial custody till October 3, following his arrest on September 18 on multiple charges, including murder, linked to the 2007 Nandigram land agitation.The latest order effectively prevents Pradhan from campaigning during the final days of the bypoll campaign, which ends on October 4.The Nandigram seat was vacated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who resigned in May and chose to retain Bhabanipur after defeating Mamata Banerjee in the assembly election held earlier this year.Meanwhile, Banerjee's decision to support Pradhan has marked a significant political shift between the Trinamool Congress and Congress in Bengal.Banerjee backed the Congress candidate after her faction's nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the October 6 contest following a meeting with Adhikari in Kolkata.Announcing her support on September 18, Banerjee described Congress as a "sister party" and a "natural ally", saying the decision was taken in the larger interest of the country and to strengthen the INDIA bloc.Banerjee also said she wanted to send a message about the future of the opposition alliance beginning from Bengal.The move follows a series of political developments involving the TMC. The Election Commission had frozen the Trinamool Congress' traditional name and ‘Jora Ghash Phul’ symbol amid an internal party dispute, assigning separate names and symbols to Banerjee's faction and its dissidents for the upcoming bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar.The Congress-TMC relationship has previously seen periods of cooperation. The parties contested the 2001 Bengal assembly election together and later joined hands in the 2009 Lok Sabha polls. In 2011, their alliance helped end the Left Front's 34-year rule in Bengal.
Article Summary: Pradhan was sent to judicial custody by a Contai court in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district. The Nandigram seat was vacated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who resigned in May and chose to retain Bhabanipur.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya will file its first chargesheet in the case on or before September 25, a CJI-led bench was informed on Monday.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the bench that the chargesheet would have to be filed as the statutory 90-day period from the first arrest in the case would lapse soon.“Ninety days from the date of the first arrest are going to be over on September 25, so we will have to file the chargesheet, otherwise, they (the accused) will get default bail,” Mehta said.The bench, comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, also perused a detailed status report submitted by the SIT in a sealed cover.Under Section 167(2) of the CrPC, an accused becomes entitled to statutory bail if the investigating agency fails to file a chargesheet in the trial court within the stipulated period of 60 or 90 days.The bench had earlier directed the probe team to complete its investigation expeditiously and take it to its logical conclusion. It had also asked the SIT to file a status report in a sealed cover on the progress of the probe into the alleged theft of donations.The Supreme court had taken note of the formation of a four-member SIT headed by IGP Kiran S to investigate the alleged embezzlement of donations and directed the Uttar Pradesh government to include a forensic auditor in the probe team.Observing that “remedial actions will have to be taken”, the bench had said steps would be taken to “ensure transparency” and directed the SIT to submit a status report.The court's directions came after allegations of irregularities surfaced in the management of donations at the Ram Temple. Several petitioners approached the Supreme Court seeking a CBI probe and a forensic audit of the temple trust’s finances.
Article Summary: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the bench that the chargesheet would have to be filed as the statutory 90-day period from the first arrest in the case would lapse soon. The bench, comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, also perused a detailed status report submitted by the SIT.

Article Title: Bihar harassment case: NCW takes suo motu cognizance, demands immediate arrest of perpetrators
Article Text:
NCW seeks immediate arrests after viral Bihar harassment video

NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Women (NCW) on Monday took suo motu cognizance of harassment and assault of a young woman and her male companion in Bihar’s Jamui district, after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.NCW chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar wrote to Bihar director general of police, calling for the immediate registration of an FIR, identification and arrest of all those involved, and a time-bound and impartial investigation.The commission has specifically asked authorities to use the video footage to identify the alleged perpetrators and take action against them.The incident reportedly took place on the evening of September 19. Bihar Police said the woman and the man were allegedly stopped and harassed by a group of people by the roadside.Jamui Police said that an FIR had been registered and SIT was formed to probe the incident. Moreover, 3 people have been taken into custody."An FIR has been registered regarding the incident of molestation and indecent behavior by anti-social elements shown in the video, and a SIT has been constituted under the leadership of the Sub-Divisional Police Officer of Jamui; the team is conducting continuous raids.Based on identifications made from the video, three individuals have been taken into custody," news agency ANI quoted SP Vishwajeet Dayal saying."Two others have been identified, and efforts are underway to arrest them as well... As for the main accused—the one who appears to have behaved indecently with the woman—he has been identified, and we are making efforts to arrest him soon; we are actively working on this... We will take action against those attempting to tarnish the reputation of Jamui district... We have arrested three minors so far; as the investigation proceeds and more individuals are taken into custody. ..," he added.According to the SP, the young man and woman are friends and attend the same coaching institute. He did not disclose additional details, saying, “We must keep some information private”.
Article Summary: NCW chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar wrote to Bihar director general of police, calling for the immediate registration of an FIR. Incident reportedly took place on the evening of September 19. Bihar Police said that an FIR had been registered and SIT was formed to probe the incident.
